# GitHub Copilot instructions

When generating, editing, reviewing, or summarizing durable prose in this repository, apply the betterwords rules from `docs/betterwords.md`.

Durable prose includes README text, docs, release notes, issue text, pull request descriptions, specs, product copy, newsletters, scripts, and slide text.

Do not apply betterwords to ordinary chat or code comments unless the user asks.

Before drafting, editing, translating, or auditing, read `docs/betterwords.md` completely: operating notes, all numbered rules, and final self-check. Recover every truncated or omitted portion in consecutive chunks before starting. Selected sections, head-and-tail excerpts, summaries, and remembered rules are insufficient. If the complete file is missing or inaccessible, state the limitation and obtain the missing text before proceeding under betterwords. Reload the complete current file if it becomes unavailable after context loss, compaction, or a version change.

Consider every rule, then apply it according to its severity, precedence, and the artifact's intent and format. Use the guidance while composing and review the complete deliverable against it afterward. Preserve strong passages and justified exceptions. The final self-check is a condensed reminder, not a substitute for the full guidance.

Deliver the requested writing or editorial findings. Do not substitute test code, lint output, a compliance score, or a checklist. Mechanical checks and read-coverage records cannot establish understanding or editorial compliance; judge the actual text in context.

Preserve supplied facts, attribution, uncertainty, scope, and required format. Do not add facts, sources, sourced quotations, numbers, product claims, or firsthand experience. Add a hypothetical example or proposed quote only when the user requests it and its status is explicit.

For drafting or rewriting, return the production text first and preserve supported voice signals, distinctive phrasing, and useful structure. For copyediting or line editing, make the minimum effective changes at the requested level and leave strong passages alone. Do not silently turn a copyedit into a rewrite. Add only brief notes about consequential changes, ambiguity, material assumptions, or unresolved source problems.

For an audit, preserve the artifact and report findings in severity order. Include the exact excerpt, rule number, explanation, and a concise proposed correction for each finding. For a grouped rule, name the specific pattern. Distinguish confirmed violations from judgment calls and explain writing-quality problems without inferring human or model authorship.

When verification and rewriting are both requested, verify claims against the sources and test the argument before polishing the prose. Do not describe an output as fact-checked unless the task included source verification. If verification was required but sources were unavailable, label the factual status as unverified.
